title: Ideal pair phase references bound all delay ranges with 1,268 tests in selected Allen mouse circuit models
abstract: We found the smallest number of ideal pair phase references that make every delay range finite within a node-time-shift family of linear circuit models. Allen Synaptic Physiology r2.1 gave 2248 selected mouse VisP edges in 1061 recordings and 309 human TCx edges in 137 recordings. The minimum totals were 1268 and 200 references. Fixing all relative node shifts instead needs 1725 and 253 references. Thus finite ranges still leave 457 and 53 shift dimensions. References are restricted to pairs with a selected chemical edge. A partition search gives exact designs; 2557 linear programs and exhaustive checks on all nonempty four-node directed graphs passed. Label and delay filters retain the distinction. Ideal unwrapped phase slopes, usable cross-spectra, independent input noise and fixed linear models are assumptions. No phase data were measured. Missing edges, selected slices and unknown measurement precision limit biological use. Code, proof, aggregate results, source hashes and external regeneration instructions are supplied. External records are not bundled.

display.caption: Exact minimum reference counts for finite delay ranges versus complete removal of relative node shifts, within the specified family. No phase references were measured.

citations.reason: Extends its whole-recording delay-range audit with exact reference design; reproduces initial counts. No prior code or tables copied.
